item.description: ### Fixed - **Approving from your phone attaches to the request the alert was about.** With more than one request waiting, a tap on the alert could land on a different one. Perch now matches the request the alert named, and refuses rather than guesses when it cannot tell them apart. - **Answering a Claude prompt at the terminal clears it everywhere.** Choosing Yes in the terminal used to leave the request on your phone and the row showing "waiting" until it timed out. Perch now sees that the approved command is running and clears both. A decision that arrives after the turn has finished no longer brings a finished session back to "waiting". - **Replying from a notification works inside tmux and herdr.** The reply used to be typed into whichever pane was active, which could be the wrong one. It is now delivered to the session's own pane, the way messages from your phone are. If Perch cannot tell which pane that is, it brings the terminal forward instead of typing anywhere. - **A phone with an old pairing code can no longer wear Perch down.** Each refused connection held on to a system resource for good. After an hour or two of a stale phone retrying, Perch could stop receiving live updates from your agents, and permission requests would stall for close to a minute each. Refused connections are now released at once, and the local socket recovers on its own if the system ever does run short.
